summary: Round 1 independent review of the allowlist amendment in the frozen uncommitted attempt03 snapshot (manifest 03bcd812...). Scheduling: node_selection.scheduler_flags (node_selection.py:79-83) emits only '--nodes=1' and '--exclude=<live partition minus allowlist>', never a multi-node --nodelist; it re-validates the record and requires sorted live sinfo membership to equal the frozen partition_nodes, so command generation fails on any membership change (prepare.py:218-222, exercised by test_node_selection PrepareCommandTests). run.sbatch is byte-identical to attempt02 (--exclusive, gpu:a100:4, 6x6 CPUs, 192G, 24 h via --time=1440). Runtime: launch.allocation (launch.py:82-116) takes the host from platform.node(), requires SLURM_JOB_NUM_NODES=1, and node_selection.selected_host requires host in the validated allowlist and scontrol NodeList exactly equal to that host; the pre-existing Exclusive=NODE / 25.11 whole-CPU + sole-occupancy gate, frozen run.sbatch Command check, partition MaxTime check, four-UUID placement and 36-core gate are unchanged. selected_node then feeds retention.json, SIM10_EXPECTED_NODE and validate_result's per-rank host check (launch.py:151); no sdfampere036 literal remains in runtime code. Hardware gate: node_selection.hardware_gate runs after hardware.inventory and before local capacity, Weka staging and any case (launch.py:257-259 vs 263, 276+); it compares live lscpu -J fields, exact sorted NIC lines from lspci -D -nn against the candidate's own inventory (inventory used lspci -Dnn, identical domain-prefixed format; verified in sdfampere010/036 raw copies), exact GPU UUID set, per-BDF NUMA/max link 16 GT/s x16 from sysfs, and driver 575.57.08 from nvidia-smi -q. Any mismatch raises before staging; no retry or node substitution exists. Evidence integrity: the nine October 26 inventory paths are hash-pinned in node_allowlist.evidence_files and duplicated in manifest.read_only_files; prepare re-hashes them, verify_manifest (prepare.py:169-176) re-hashes every read-only file, requires node is None for schema 2, re-runs node_selection.profile on each inventory and requires equality with the embedded normalized profile, so a 'latest file' or edited profile cannot be substituted. Candidate qualification is conservative: 33 of 42 partition nodes are excluded with recorded reasons (DOWN/DRAIN/MAINTENANCE/RESERVED states, Gres not gpu:a100:4, Gen3 or non-x4 scratch links, NIC layout mismatch, incomplete inventory, and the malformed sdfampere040 JSON which was caught as a ValueError). The allowlist is labelled candidate qualification only; availability remains 'unconfirmed'. Workload invariance: plan.py, runner.py, run.sbatch, stages.py, reference.py, mpi_cube.py, gpu_guards.py and all historical helpers have the same hashes as manifest-02; cases, controls, resources, budget (75072 s within 86400 s), retention and local_required_bytes match attempt02; verify_manifest still enforces cases==matrix(), controls and resources. Legacy compatibility: schema 1 manifests still verify (schema_version in (1,2), allowlist forbidden on schema 1) and command emits --nodelist for them; a review receipt is bound to the exact manifest hash, so review-02 (93d5fdcb...) cannot be applied to this changed snapshot. Native caveat: pr_sha, receipt hash, pr_source and the psana/meson.build mismatch disposition accepted in review-02 are unchanged and the amendment touches no native or GPU path; this review preserves that acceptance for preparation only. Host evidence: checks-allowlist-01.json reports 84/84 CPU-only tests (log shows all 20 node-selection tests), 16 AST parses, bash syntax and diff checks, and references the unchanged host-native-check-02 receipt; CUDA/MPI/full-shape checks remain allocation gates and nothing has executed. IMPL-R2-001 and IMPL-R2-002 remain deferred and unfixed. Findings ALLOW-R1-001..004 are nonblocking hardening/operational notes. No submission is authorized by this review.

The original inventory files under ampere-inventory-20261026-r1 are outside the permitted roots; I inspected the copies in allowlist-checks/inventory and could not independently confirm their SHA256 against the manifest hashes.

findings.evidence: SIM10_EXPECTED_NODE is set to selected_node in the case environment, but no consumer exists: grep of all .py files under notes/ finds only this assignment; runner.py never reads it. Rank host identity is enforced only after each case completes, by validate_result (launch.py:151) comparing row['host'] to selected_node. This is the pre-existing attempt02 design (baseline launch.py:262 set it from manifest['node'] with the same absence of a consumer), so the amendment introduces no regression, but ALLOWLIST.md line 47-48 presents the environment setting as part of the node enforcement.
findings.requested_change: Either document in ALLOWLIST.md that SIM10_EXPECTED_NODE is informational and the enforced check is validate_result's per-rank host comparison, or in a future reviewed snapshot have runner.py require platform.node().split('.')[0] == os.environ['SIM10_EXPECTED_NODE'] before the timing barrier. No change to runner.py is authorised in this amendment; do not alter the frozen hash set for this round.

findings.evidence: hardware_gate verifies live CPU, NIC, GPU UUID, GPU PCI/NUMA/link and driver, and its receipt scope string says local capacity is checked separately. Local scratch is only checked by local_capacity (mount target /lscratch, xfs/ext4, free bytes). The inventoried RAID0 two-drive Gen4 x4 layout and NVMe model that qualified the candidate at preparation time are not re-compared live, although hardware.inventory records nvme_controllers and block_devices in hardware.json. Because local storage is used only for untimed cube export and capacity is gated, this is not a correctness risk.
findings.requested_change: Optional hardening for a later snapshot: compare live nvme controller model/firmware and md0 raid0 slave count from hardware.json against candidates[host].profile.local_scratch in the qualification receipt, or state explicitly in ALLOWLIST.md that local scratch identity is preparation-time only and export timing on a different SSD is recorded, not compared.

findings.evidence: The unit fixtures use NIC lines without the PCI domain prefix ('02:00.0 Ethernet controller [0200]: ConnectX-6') and synthetic lscpu JSON, and no test exercises node_selection.profile() or the schema-2 verify_manifest path against a real inventory record. The real-format compatibility (inventory lspci -Dnn versus runtime lspci -D -nn, lscpu -J field/data rows, sysfs '16.0 GT/s PCIe' strings) is correct by my inspection of hardware.py:35-48 and the sdfampere010/036 inventory copies, but it is not regression-tested; a future change to either command's flags would make the live NIC gate fail closed on every node without a test catching it.
findings.requested_change: Add CPU-only tests that load one real inventory copy (e.g. allowlist-checks/inventory/sdfampere010-41998196.json) through profile() and assert the normalized profile equals the manifest candidate, and that hardware_gate accepts a hardware record built from the same inventory's lspci/lscpu text. Nonblocking; no change to the frozen snapshot is required this round.

findings.evidence: Candidate selection freezes a Slurm-state snapshot from 2026-11-15T20:14Z: nodes with four GPUs that were in MAINTENANCE/RESERVED at observation (sdfampere024, sdfampere039) are permanently excluded, and candidates are only compared to October 26 inventory. sdfampere016-019 were re-imaged on 2026-11-12 with a different kernel; if any of the nine candidates receives a driver or lspci database update before the job starts, hardware_gate raises 'Live driver drift' or 'Live NIC inventory drift' and the campaign ends before staging after the queue wait. This is correct fail-closed behaviour and matches the stated purpose, but it is an operational completion risk in addition to IMPL-R2-001/002.
findings.requested_change: Before authorising submission, re-run frozen 'prepare.py command' as ALLOWLIST.md instructs and, if a long queue wait is expected, consider refreshing the allowlist snapshot (new prepare + review round) so exclusions and driver expectations reflect current node state. Do not relax the live gates.
